system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 10-39 (19 letters scrambled plus two extra vowel sets), tilde for doubling, word codes and a nomenclature from 40.

diacritics.note: tilde over a figure doubles the letter (ll, nn, ss, ee)

system.notes: a has a fourth sign (39); 40 = de, 42 = la; ten nomenclature codes identified with Avenel's footnotes; nine more names and 41 = que added in Nov 2026 from his notes on the sibling letters (texts/key.md, Extension).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: 'la', 'd'autres', 'd'elle ... elle' (tilde = doubling), 'Brassac', 'l'ambassade' placed beside clear words.
Remaining letters from further words; alphabet and homophones recovered.
Avenel 1858 found to print both letters deciphered, with his reconstructed key.
Reading agrees with Avenel word for word; nomenclature codes resolved from his footnotes.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the cryptiana transcription; saved the final.py decryption; copied the Avenel reading and the key table from SOLUTION.md to texts/

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the two entries read: the raw decode of the partial transcription does not join into sentences (decoded, not read); Avenel's printed text reads (A, excerpt note added). Class already solved kept.

Re-reading (batch b33): DECODE R9461 and R9462 fetched with the project cookie: three colour scans, no attachment, transcription or comment; Avenel, Lettres de Richelieu III, pp. 367-386 fetched as Google Books page images (OIQItRIybmIC).
Avenel nos. CXCIX and CCV transcribed in full from the page images, with his printed figures and footnote decipherments (texts/ff87-89_avenel_figures.txt).

Every run of Avenel's printed figures decoded with the recovered key (research/reading_audit/b33_rl_decode.py): all agree with his footnotes; figure 39 corrected from a to et (both occurrences, 'frontiere et menee', 'Chevreuse et autres'); two figure slips (16 in 'menee au', final 29 in 'ambassada').

Three places checked on the manuscript scans: the clerk omitted the a of 'au' (Avenel's 16 is a misprint); f. 89v has 'a 51 30 18 52' (au roy et a la reyne mere), Avenel printed only 51; the second Brassac has the doubling stroke.

Running reading of both letters (texts/ff87-89_reading.md, English ff87-89_en.md): Avenel's clear text, ciphered words in the figures' spelling, codes named from his footnotes; body 0.826 clean sentences (b17 fr), 0.971 explicit holes only; entry 0 decoded, not read -> read (A).

Leads 1577 and 2744 (and issue #206): Avenel t. III prints nine sibling letters of Feb-May 1629 (nos. CXIX, CXXXV, CXLVI, CXLVII, CLIII, CLIV, CLV, CLVIII, CLXVII; BnF fr. 3828, 3825, 3835, tied by their Béthune numbers) with the figures in place and his decipherment in footnotes. Brice Dudout, with Claude Opus 5.5.

Figures of the nine letters read from the page images of archive.org lettresinstructi03richuoft, checked against two OCRs; no change after re-reading the disagreements (texts/fr3828_avenel_figures.txt).

Pre-registered test of the fr. 3829 key (final.py @ 9736c436, unchanged) on held-out CLIV + CLV (333 figures) against Avenel's footnotes: agreement 0.940, best of 200 shuffled tables 0.456; threshold 0.85 and best + 0.30 (fr3828_measure/).

All runs of the nine letters decoded and read (texts/fr3828_reading.md, fr3828_en.md): 368 of 374 cipher words read (0.984); four small differences with Avenel's glosses (mécontent, la dégast, en veule, septembra); key extended with 41 = que and nine names from Avenel's notes outside the test letters (texts/key.md); 40 used as a syllable, 20 as the number in 'le 20 mai'.

Strict count (owner's decision on #813, 19 Nov 2026): the ten values from Avenel's notes and the context readings of 59 (CLVIII) and 84 (CLIV) counted as holes: 352 of 374 cipher words (0.941); CLIII, CLIV, CLVIII, CLXVII read in part; CXLVII read by the short-text floor (fr3828_measure/word_count.tsv).

outcome.notes: Independent ciphertext-only recovery, later matched to Avenel's 1858 decipherment; Brassac's appointment to Rome in 1630 confirms. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the raw key decode was decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026, re-reading: Avenel's text transcribed in full with his printed figures, every run decoded with the key and three places checked on the manuscript; both letters read (texts/ff87-89_reading.md). Class already solved kept. 19 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout, with Claude Opus 5.5; leads 1577, 2744): the nine sibling letters of Feb-May 1629 that Avenel prints with their figures (BnF fr. 3828, 3825, 3835) were read with this key after a pre-registered held-out test (0.940 vs best control 0.456): existing (Avenel 1858), verified with the key; key extended with ten values from his footnotes. 20 Nov 2026, strict count (owner's decision on #813: a code value fixed from the printed decipherment of the same letters, or from context, is a hole): 352 of 374 cipher words, five letters read (CXLVII by the short-text floor), four read in part (CLIII, CLIV, CLVIII, CLXVII). The manuscripts were not seen.

texts.label: ff. 87 and 89 (7 and mid-July 1629), recovered key applied
texts.summary: Richelieu to M. de Rancé, July 1629: the King's anger at Bonneuil, a wish that the Duchesse de Chevreuse be seized near the frontier and taken to Vincennes, the cabals of Lorraine with Spain; and in mid-July the stalled peace with England, Henrietta Maria's French bishop and priests, and Brassac proposed for the Rome embassy.

reading_review.note: Both letters in full from Avenel 1858 (nos. CXCIX, CCV), transcribed from the page images with his printed figures; every run decoded with the recovered key gives his footnote decipherment; three places checked on the DECODE scans (Avenel's misprinted 16 in 'menée au', his omitted 'et 52' on f. 89v). Body 0.83 clean sentences (b17 fr), 0.97 explicit holes only; one hole.

texts.label: fr. 3835 no. 15, [15 (?) Feb 1629] (Avenel no. CXIX), fr. 3829 key applied
texts.summary: Richelieu to Rancé on the Queen Mother's household and patronage: Bérulle's promise not to unite benefices to his congregation, the Queen Mother's ill-judged letter to the Parlement, Saint-Malo for the Keeper of the Seals, a pension for La Racinière, and Mme de Vendôme's nights at Vincennes.
texts.note: 51 cipher words, 2 holes (68 le cardinal de Bérulle, 69 le garde des sceaux: values from Avenel's notes, key.md Extension). Count over cipher words only (fr3828_measure/count_words.py), strict count (#813, 19 Nov 2026: a code value fixed from Avenel's notes on the same letters, or from context, is a hole). Existing: Avenel 1858 prints the decipherment; checked here with the key.

texts.label: fr. 3825 no. 28, 21 Mar [1629], Susa (Avenel no. CXXXV), fr. 3829 key applied
texts.summary: News from Susa a fortnight after the forcing of the pass: a report that the Queen Mother has had Mme de Longueville and Marie de Gonzague put in Vincennes, and advice to speak of the King's victories with modesty so as not to provoke Spain.
texts.note: 24 cipher words, no hole. Avenel's note to this letter says he rebuilt the cipher from Affaires étrangères documents. texts.label: fr. 3828 no. 17, 29 Apr 1629, Susa (Avenel no. CLIII), fr. 3829 key applied
texts.summary: To the Queen Mother: suspicions of Savoy keep Richelieu at Susa with the army; the King goes to besiege Privas, Condé is to lay waste round Montauban, and the peace with England is made but must be kept quiet until 20 May. She is to have the letter deciphered by Rancé.
